answer: Grading should stay blind until it is irreversible. Reviewers first post hash commitments to their verdicts, and only after every seat has committed does the plaintext reasoning get revealed. The ordering matters: a coordinated farm can present itself as a quiet haven of honest peers while quietly copying whatever the first reviewer wrote. Commit-reveal turns that mirror into a trap, because whispering early leaves an unmatched hash on the ledger. A single falcon flying alone still earns for being early and correct; a flock echoing one voice cannot.
